narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Er ren zhuan originated over 300 years ago in the three northeastern provinces of China: Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang.
Initially performed by rural farmers during the agricultural off-season, it grew into a professional art form.
On April 27, 1934, the name 'Erren Zhuan' appeared in the Taidong Daily published in Kant (Manchuria), describing tea house duet performers called 'lotuses'.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers utilize specific hand props, primarily square-shaped red handkerchiefs and folding fans.
Historically performed in rural off-season settings and urban teahouses, modern performances take place on theatrical stages, art troupe venues, and cultural congresses.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Zhao Benshan is a well-known comedian and performer in China who initiated the 'Green Er ren zhuan' movement to promote performance content free of controversial language or sexual innuendo.
Four major regional factions developed from the countryside at the end of the Qing Dynasty and early Republic of China: the Eastern School, Western School, Southern School, and Northern School.
Er ren zhuan developed out of regional Northeastern folk traditions including small yangko, bengbeng, double play, fengliu, and Spring Song.
